messages:
Becky Tran: notice a cluster-wide bump in attach latency in us-west2 starting ~02:10 UTC. Several launches timeout. Filing here.
Liam O'Connor: logs? cohort or node list?
Becky Tran: initial scatter: gnode-2201, gnode-2233, gnode-2244. nvme iostat shows tiny-write storm.
Harpreet Singh: DevOps-Bot reported background scrub on pool west2-scratch-3 at 02:09. DevOps-Bot: 'scrub_trigger cohort=west2-scratch-3 removed=8.9k files peak_iops=93k duration=41s'
DevOps-Bot: scrub_trigger scheduled by scrub-scheduler; cohort=west2-scratch-3; removed=8900; peak_iops=93000; dur=41s
Becky Tran: avgqu-sz hit ~420 on nvme0n1, await climbed to 52ms on affected hosts
Liam O'Connor: that's above our attach tolerance (20ms). Could cause ENOMEDIUM type drops.
Harpreet Singh: suggestion: quickly reduce scrub concurrency to 25% for west2-scratch-3 and apply io.weight cap to scrub systemd slice.
Nina Gomez: doing retention-scheduler update now. Applying 0.25 concurrency.
DevOps-Bot: retention-scheduler: set concurrency=0.25 for cohort=west2-scratch-3 (applied)
Liam O'Connor: I'm patching janitor to be attach-aware: if attach failures > 10% then throttle more aggressively. Rolling to canary nodes.
Harpreet Singh: also check if overlayfs compaction coincided.
Becky Tran: overlay compaction started 02:07 on some hosts, yes. compaction + scrub overlap looks likely.
Nina Gomez: canary results: after caps, iostat avgqu-sz down to 28 and await ~4.1ms
Becky Tran: attach success improved from 64% -> 96% on canary nodes
DevOps-Bot: Incident INC-2078 created: 'us-west2 NVMe scrub storm causing attach latencies' Severity=P2 Owners=Becky Tran, Liam O'Connor
Liam O'Connor: keeping incident open for 2h to validate. Will add runbook entry to avoid compaction+scrub overlap and add cohort-level iops limits to scheduler.
Harpreet Singh: long-term: consider background janitor QoS via kernel blk-iopoll hints and per-process io_uring limits.
Becky Tran: thanks everyone, updating downstream ML infra teams. :white_check_mark:
